title: Heer Ranjha
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Heer
cast.description: Young woman, beautiful, fiery and defiant

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Punjabi tradition. Its most famous telling is the verse of the Sufi poet Waris Shah, written in 1766. It is called... Heer Ranjha.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dhido Ranjha was the youngest of eight brothers in Takht Hazara, on the Chenab. He played the flute more often than he worked. When his father died, his brothers cheated him of good land... and one morning, he took his flute and walked away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He crossed the river to Jhang, where the chieftain's daughter Heer was the most beautiful girl in the Punjab. Ranjha fell asleep on her boat, and she woke him in a fury.

lines.speaker: heer
lines.text: [angry] Who are you, sleeping on MY boat?

lines.speaker: ranjha
lines.text: [dreamy, smiling] Someone who just woke to the most beautiful sight on the Chenab.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] By the end of the argument... they were in love.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: To stay near her, Ranjha became a cowherd for her father. Every day he took the buffaloes to graze by the river, and every day Heer brought him churi, crumbled bread with butter and sugar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [softly] They met among the trees while he played the flute.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [darker] But Heer's uncle Kaido, lame and spiteful, spied on them.

lines.speaker: kaido
lines.text: [sinister] Brother, your daughter shames us. With a cowherd. Every day by the river.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Furious, her family married Heer by force to Saida Khera, a man from another village. The qazi read the vows... while Heer refused to say them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [sorrowful] Ranjha, broken-hearted, went to the hermitage at Tilla Jogian. He had his ears pierced and became a jogi, a wandering ascetic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He went begging from door to door in the Kheras' village, until he found Heer. With the help of Saida's sister Sehti, the lovers escaped.

lines.speaker: heer
lines.text: [breathless, joyful] Ranjha! I knew you would come.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They were caught, brought before the raja, and at last allowed to marry. Heer's family pretended to welcome them home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [grave] But on the day of the wedding, Kaido poisoned her sweets. [long pause] Heer died.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [heartbroken] When Ranjha heard, he ate the poisoned sweets too... and died beside her.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [gently] Waris Shah's verse is still quoted in Lahore and Amritsar alike, a love story that belongs to both sides of the border. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
